paragraphs: LLMC is a nonprofit library consortium that provides access to global legal and historical documents through its database. The organization was founded in 1976 as a nonprofit cooperative of libraries dedicated to preserving legal and government materials. Early work used microform, and LLMC supplied libraries with reproductions of aging and at-risk legal collections.

The LLMC Digital database launched in 2003 and expanded access to rare legal titles including historical statutes, session laws, judicial decisions, administrative regulations, and government reports. Source types in the archive include Attorney General Publications, House & Senate Journals, and Treaties & Arbitrations. Special collections named on the site include the Yale Blackstone Collection, the Drew Days III Archive, and Early State Records.

The collection is described as a resource for students, historians, researchers, attorneys, and scholars. Access runs through a member portal, and an Open Access collection is offered to the public. LLMC works in partnership with hundreds of libraries and institutions to identify, preserve, and digitize historic, legal, and governmental records.
